title: Long-read sequencing reveals pre-meiotic gene conversion in sperm.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded exports/260730.recombination_events.xlsx (2.4 MB) from the authors' GitHub repository (MIT licence, also archived as Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21970165). Sheet 'Data' has 17,861 rows x 20 columns and sheet 'Legend' documents all 20 columns. Counts by dataset: TwinsUK has 4,813 CO (crossover), 1,547 NCO (non-crossover), 5,739 ambiguous and 184 complex events; SL has 2,330 / 835 / 1,846 / 35; Platinum (blood) has 11 / 369 / 143 / 9. That is 27 sample labels in total. Sperm totals are 7,143 CO, 2,382 NCO, 219 complex and 7,585 ambiguous, which match the paper exactly. Only 2 duplicate positions. Every row is a detected recombination event: reads with no event are not in the table. event_type is derived from the snp_alleles column by counting haplotype switches.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Raw PacBio long reads: TwinsUK reads are on EGA (EGAD00001015736, controlled access), SL reads are only available on request, and Platinum reads are on dbGaP or AWS. The 196,296,004 quality-filtered reads that form the background (reads with no event) are described in the paper but were not downloaded. The supplementary tables were not retrievable (Europe PMC timed out). The existing-models search was skipped because Part A failed.

a1_downloadable.note: The processed event table downloads openly from GitHub/Zenodo under an MIT licence (checked). The raw reads are controlled (EGA) or on request (SL), so any project that needs the background reads fails here.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The table holds only detected events, with no negatives. Predicting where gene conversion happens would mean building background (non-event) windows from the controlled raw reads or from the genome. The scientifically interesting label, PRDM9-driven NCO versus the pre-meiotic NCO component, is a latent mixture component and not a column (checked).

a3_inputs_present.note: Genomic coordinates in GRCh37, GRCh38 and T2T are present, so DNA sequence context can be pulled from public reference genomes without lookups (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: The Legend sheet states units: read length in bp, genetic length in cM (centimorgans), rate in cM/bp (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: 17,861 events in total, but only 2,751 NCOs (2,382 in sperm, 369 in blood), the class the paper is about (checked).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Sperm CO/NCO/complex/ambiguous counts of 7,143 / 2,382 / 219 / 7,585 and the blood counts of 11 / 369 / 9 / 143 match the paper text exactly (checked).

a8_label_provenance.note: The available label column, event_type (CO / NCO / complex / ambiguous), is a deterministic rule on the number of haplotype switches in snp_alleles, which is itself a column. Predicting it from the table is leakage by construction (checked against the paper's Methods).

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around sites in sperm to predict whether short gene-conversion events happen there, and whether they arise before meiosis.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence context around the 2,751 detected non-crossover events, plus background sites. The background sites would have to be built, because the open table lists only events.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a site carries a gene-conversion event, or which mechanism caused it. The paper's mechanism split is a statistical mixture, not a measured label per event.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Researchers studying meiosis and germline mutation would get a map of where pre-meiotic gene conversion happens. Without negatives or a per-event mechanism label, the model can't be trained honestly.

ml_idea: Considered: classify NCO events as PRDM9-hotspot-driven versus pre-meiotic from sequence context (for example DNABERT-2 embeddings), or predict event location versus background. The open table has no negatives and no per-event mechanism label, and event_type is computed from the SNP-allele column.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the table contains any rows for reads without an event. It contains none, so the location task has no negatives.

verdict_reason: The open table (17,861 rows, counts match the paper) lists only detected recombination events. It has no negatives, and the non-event reads are controlled on EGA or available only on request (A2). The only label column, event_type, is computed from the haplotype-switch column (A8). The mechanism of interest is a latent mixture component, not a per-event label.
